fields.title: What Does Modi-Meloni’s ‘Melodi’ Frenzy Have To Do With Earring Sales In Bengaluru?
fields.short_description: A Bengaluru-based acrylic jewellery startup has found itself to be the unintended beneficiary of the internet's continued obsession with the 'Melodi' phenomenon
fields.blog_body:
In a butterfly effect of sorts, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Italian counterpart Giorgia Meloni’s viral ‘Melodi’ moment last month has ended up boosting the sales of a Bengaluru startup that manufactures acrylic jewellery. But what does PM Modi gifting a box of Melody toffees to Meloni have to do with a jewellery startup?

Well, the startup in question, Rainbow Hues, specialises in creating wearable accessories inspired by iconic Indian treats from the 1990s and early 2000s. Its catalogue includes earrings modelled after Melody toffees, Kismi bars, Hajmola tablets and Kaccha Mango Bite candies. While the concept taps into nostalgia for millennials who grew up with these snacks, one product in particular has found itself riding a fresh wave of internet fame.

According to a report in Deccan Herald, Rainbow Hues recorded a 40% jump in sales after Meloni posted a video on May 20 showing PM Modi gifting her a packet of Melody toffees. The report quoted founder Rebecca Mendonza as saying that the startup’s Melody earrings sold out within 24 hours of the video going online, and replenishing inventory took nearly a week.

fields.title: Best Vegetarian Protein Foods to Hit 120g Daily: Paneer, Soy, Pulses & More
fields.short_description: No powders, no meat: hitting 120g of protein daily on a vegetarian diet is possible with dairy, soy, pulses, nuts, and smart meal planning, says expert Edwina Raj.
fields.blog_body:
For many vegetarians, meeting high protein goals can feel like a challenge, especially if they want to avoid powders, shakes, or meat substitutes. Yet Edwina insists it’s absolutely possible to hit 120 grams of protein daily with smart food choices and balanced planning.

In a feature published by The Indian Express, Edwina Raj, Head of Clinical Nutrition & Dietetics in Bangalore, highlights that the secret to meeting protein goals lies in variety and in spreading intake across meals.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommends around 0.8–1.2 grams of protein per kilogram of body weight, but those who strength‑train or engage in intense workouts often need more. Here are 5 ways of how to hit 120g of daily protein on a pure vegetarian diet.

Dairy Delivers Big Gains

Dairy products remain one of the simplest ways for vegetarians to add protein. Two glasses of milk can provide about 16 grams, while a bowl of curd contributes another 8–10 grams. Paneer is especially rich, offering nearly 18 grams per 100 g serving. Greek yoghurt or hung curd are also excellent options, giving a thicker texture and higher protein punch. Including dairy in breakfast or lunch ensures a steady start to the day’s protein count.

fields.title: Tea Time Mistakes: 5 Foods You Should Stop Pairing With Your Daily Chai
fields.short_description: Before you sip your tea, read this. Know how pairing tea with these foods may spoil taste and affect digestion.
fields.blog_body:
Many people drink tea as soon as they wake up or after returning home. Tea is an important part of daily life in India, but experts suggest being careful about what you consume with it, as certain combinations may not be suitable.

Spicy And Strong-Flavoured Foods: Highly spicy or strongly flavoured foods such as garlic, onion, hot sauce, curry and chilli can overpower the taste of tea. This can affect the aroma and flavour balance, making it difficult to enjoy the drink fully.

Lemon With Tea: Adding lemon juice to tea is not recommended. It may cause acidity and diarrhoea in some individuals. People who have the habit of consuming lemon immediately after tea are advised to avoid this combination.

Chocolate: Chocolate does not pair well with tea as its rich sweetness can mask the natural flavour of the beverage. However, it may be better suited with black tea rather than milk tea for a more balanced taste experience.

fields.title: 'AI Is Not A Mortal Threat, But A Significant Opportunity': TCS Chairman N Chandrasekaran
fields.short_description: Some say AI poses a fundamental threat... I see it differently: far from being a mortal threat, AI is the most significant opportunity yet for enterprise IT,' says Chandra.
fields.blog_body:
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) Chairman N Chandrasekaran on June 9 sought to allay concerns over the impact of artificial intelligence (AI) on the IT services industry, saying that AI represents a major growth opportunity rather than an existential threat.

Addressing shareholders at TCS’ 31st Annual General Meeting, Chandrasekaran said AI is poised to expand the global technology market and create new business opportunities for IT

“Some say AI poses a fundamental threat to that model. I see it differently: far from being a mortal threat, AI is the most significant opportunity yet for enterprise IT," Chandrasekaran said.

He noted that concerns over AI intensified after agentic AI systems began demonstrating capabilities such as writing code, testing software and managing technology operations.

“In late 2024, Agentic AI systems began to look genuinely ready for enterprise workflows — writing code, testing software, running technology operations. A serious question crystallised: if AI can do this work, what happens to an industry built around doing it?" he said.

Muskan Chaudhary has emerged as the topper in the Rajasthan Pre-DLed 2026 exam. She is a resident of Sriganganagar. Chanchal Vaishnav from Ajmer is in second place. Tilok Bairagi has secured third place.

The Rajasthan BSTC exam took place on May 20, 2026, at various centres across the state. It was an OMR-based exam, and candidates were allotted three hours to complete it. fields.title: Corporate America Is Starting To Ration AI As Costs Explode Despite The Boom: What's Happening
fields.short_description: Uber, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and DoorDash curb AI use as soaring token costs blow budgets, shifting from tokenmaxxing to stricter, results driven deployment.
fields.blog_body:
For the past two years, companies across the United States rushed to embrace artificial intelligence, encouraging employees to use AI tools for everything from coding and research to customer service and productivity. But now, some of America’s biggest corporations are beginning to slow down and place limits on AI usage as costs spiral far beyond expectations.

According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, executives at major firms including Uber, Meta, Microsoft, Salesforce and DoorDash are increasingly trying to control AI spending after seeing usage costs surge dramatically. Some companies reportedly exhausted annual AI budgets within just a few months, while others saw expenses double or even triple as employees embraced AI tools at scale.

fields.title: How To Use UPI Without Internet: A Simple Step-By-Step Guide
fields.short_description: Offline UPI services can be extremely useful during poor internet connectivity, emergencies, or while travelling in remote areas where mobile data may not work properly.
fields.blog_body:
Most people use UPI payments through apps like Google Pay, PhonePe, or Paytm with an internet connection. But did you know you can also send money through UPI even without mobile data or Wi-Fi? The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) allows users to access basic UPI services offline using a simple USSD-based feature on feature phones and smartphones alike.

Before using offline UPI services, make sure your mobile number is linked to your bank account, UPI services are activated on your number, and you have a working mobile network signal for SMS and calls. 

Step 1: Dial *99#
Open your phone’s dialer and type *99# from the mobile number linked to your bank account. This service works across most banks in India. 

Step 2: Choose the ‘Send Money’ Option
After dialing, a menu will appear on your screen with several banking options such as Send Money, Request Money, Check Balance, and My Profile. Select the “Send Money” option by entering the corresponding number.

Step 3: Select How You Want to Send Money
You can transfer money using UPI ID, mobile number, bank account and IFSC code. Choose the method you prefer.

fields.title: AI Cost Crunch: Microsoft Cutting Claude Code Access, Redirecting Engineers To GitHub Copilot CLI
fields.short_description: The core catalyst behind the reported rollback is the volatile pricing structure inherent to agentic AI workflows
fields.blog_body:
In a move highlighting the escalating financial reality of generative software engineering, Microsoft is reportedly stripping internal access to Anthropic’s Claude Code. According to internal communications, the technology giant is systematically cancelling employee licences for the popular terminal-based assistant, mandating that its software engineers transition fully to its proprietary alternative, GitHub Copilot CLI.

The reversal marks an unexpected shift in Microsoft’s internal development strategy. Just six months ago, the company expanded access to Claude Code across its Experiences + Devices division—the massive unit tasked with building Windows, Microsoft 365, Teams, and Surface hardware. The initiative allowed thousands of developers, designers, and project managers to run parallel trials comparing the two AI assistants. However, the sheer popularity of the Anthropic-powered engine triggered an unpredicted surge in operational expenses, forcing executives to intervene before the conclusion of the financial year on June 30.

fields.title: GK: Which Is The Wettest Place In The World? 99% People Fail To Answer Correctly
fields.short_description: This place in Meghalaya holds the record as the world's wettest inhabited place, receiving nearly 11,871 mm of rain annually. Here's how locals thrive amid constant downpours
fields.blog_body:
For many people, rain brings relief from scorching summer temperatures and is often associated with romance and beauty. But what would life be like if it rained almost every day of the year? Nestled in the East Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, Mawsynram is officially recognised as the wettest inhabited place on Earth. (Image-AI)

While Cherrapunji was once known worldwide for receiving the highest rainfall, Mawsynram has now overtaken its famous neighbour by a narrow margin, earning the distinction of being the rainiest place on the planet. Located roughly 16 kilometres from Cherrapunji, Mawsynram records an average annual rainfall of around 11,871 millimetres. Although it does not rain throughout the year, showers are a near-daily occurrence.

Nearly 90% of the village's annual rainfall is concentrated within a six-month period, with July typically witnessing the heaviest downpours. The village's extraordinary rainfall is largely due to its unique geographical location. Moisture-laden winds from the Bay of Bengal are forced upward when they encounter the surrounding hills. As the air cools, dense clouds form and release intense rainfall, creating ideal conditions for one of the wettest climates on Earth.
